ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.by: KERNEL_BUILDER-20260903-213930 (orchestrator, on Operator instruction to resolve it on product grounds)
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.question: The implementer refused to claim the tripwire exemption for knowledge_code_index_tests.rs:265, which holds PostgreSQL DDL (BIGSERIAL, public.users), and escalated rather than widening the exemption quietly. Correct call - it is not a tripwire.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.inspected: MIGRATION_SQL sits in a block with PKG_JSON, JSON_SCHEMA and BROKEN_RUST, one fixture per language, consumed by mt097_adapter_parses_each_language_and_versions. It is the code indexer's parser corpus.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.ruling: EXEMPT under a newly named third category, content-as-data. It is neither a tripwire nor a violation. Handshake's code indexer exists to index the user's repository, and real repositories contain SQL. This fixture is how the product proves it can parse a .sql file, exactly as PKG_JSON proves it can parse package.json. The PostgreSQL flavour of the DDL is incidental - it is representative user content, not a statement about Handshake's own storage.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.why_scrubbing_it_would_be_the_wrong_outc: Removing it would not make the product less dependent on PostgreSQL, because it never was here. It would delete the only proof that the indexer handles SQL, degrading a real product capability to satisfy a rule aimed at something else. Governance would be damaging the thing it exists to protect.
ac_141_1_ruling_2026_09_06.anti_laundering_test: The exemption is deliberately hard to abuse: the tokens must live inside a string literal or fixture file used as parser input, and must not appear in an import, dependency, feature gate, env var, connection string, or any code path. If a token can influence how the process talks to a database, it is a dependency and exemption (b) does not apply. A future reader can apply that test mechanically.
